solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Winner of event? Just second

parts.note: the winner of an event is the one who comes first; but just the second letter of the word 'event' is V, whose NATO phonetic-alphabet name is the champion's own title

explanation.surface: Someone asks who won the competition and is told, curtly, that they merely came second.
explanation.walkthrough: The second letter of 'event' is V, and in the radio alphabet V is spoken as this word, which also means a winner. 'Just second' seems to undercut the winner, but it means 'only the second letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion or conqueror is one who triumphs, the plain sense of this word, which also names V in the radio alphabet.

clue.text: Guarantee? You'll need this for using coupon without hesitation

indicators.note: without tells us to take the hesitation sound away from the coupon word

parts.note: a voucher is a coupon
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A shop assistant tells a customer that a coupon will be needed to get the deal, and to hand it over promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch for something is to guarantee it, a verb of assurance.

clue.text: Firmly establishes setter that's heading for success

parts.note: cement is a setter: it is something that sets hard

indicators.note: the heading for a word is its first letter, so take the start of 'success'

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is said to be on the way to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is a substance that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: To cement a relationship or position is to fix it securely, a figurative use.

clue.text: Most stubbly face disguised by oxygen mask

indicators.note: by means next to, so the oxygen symbol stands beside the rearranged letters

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: disguised means changed in appearance, so these letters are rearranged
most of the word stubbly is kept: its first four letters stay and the last three go

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A very bristly face is hidden behind an oxygen mask, as in a hospital scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' keeps the first four of the seven letters of 'stubbly'; 'disguised' then rearranges them with the next word. 'Mask' looks like the oxygen mask but is the verb defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure or conceal the meaning of something is to mask it, a verb of concealment.

clue.text: One of two identical bits of research into cooks' receding gums?

indicators.note: into means the single letter goes inside the reversed word
receding means going backwards, so the word for cooks' dishes is read in reverse

parts.note: stews are what cooks make; also, to stew is to cook

parts.words: One of two identical bits of research
parts.note: the word research contains two E's; one of them is used

explanation.surface: A scientific study looks into why cooks' gums are shrinking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receding gums' suggests dentistry, but 'receding' turns STEWS into SWETS and 'gums' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gums are chewy confectionery, so they are a kind of candy, plural like the answer.

clue.text: Start with a victory before the City comeback?

indicators.note: before puts the victory word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the City's letters are read backwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A sports report: an early win before a comeback by Manchester City or another 'City' team.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postcode is EC; reversed it is CE. 'Start' is a flinch, not a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or flinch suddenly, which is what one does when grimacing in pain.

clue.text: What's said on passing around hat and pipe

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A collection is taken with a hat and a pipe passed around the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like handing round the hat, but it means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tombstone is words spoken or written about someone who has died, that is, passed on.

clue.text: Where two poisoned former PM

definitions.meaning: the English cathedral city where Sergei and Yulia Skripal were poisoned with a nerve agent in 2018
the Marquess of this title was a Victorian British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A news item about a former Prime Minister poisoning two people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marquess of Salisbury was Prime Minister three times between 1885 and 1902; the city, in Wiltshire, saw the 2018 Novichok attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city in Wiltshire and the Victorian Tory premier share the one name.

clue.text: Parent eats one fine preserve

indicators.note: eats means the parent word swallows the other letters inside it

parts.note: mummy is a parent, a mother
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A mother eats a fine jar of jam or other preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a jam, but it is the verb defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body, as in ancient Egypt, is to preserve it from decay.

clue.text: Where one might see cowslips too!

definitions.text: Where one might see cowslips too!

parts.words: Where one might see cowslips too!
parts.note: cowslips are wildflowers of the meadow, and slips are cricket fielders who stand near the batsman

explanation.surface: A nature lover points out the spot where cowslips grow as well.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips stand close to the bat, in the part of the ground nearest the pitch; the wildflower cowslip grows 'in field' too.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielding area close to the wicket is where the slips stand, and wild cowslips grow in a meadow.

clue.text: Sponsor hated frog jumping around

indicators.note: jumping around suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sponsor who hated a frog that was leaping about.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening a male sponsor vouches for the child, the religious role of this word.

clue.text: Fake gem, a mix of nine others

indicators.note: a mix of means the letters of these words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A counterfeit jewel is made by mixing nine other stones.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an imitation diamond made of paste or glass, a cheap sparkly stone.

clue.text: Real soapstone content, as well

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the letters sit inside the words real soapstone

explanation.surface: Something is made of genuine soapstone too.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and in addition are synonyms of the definition, an adverb of addition.

clue.text: Adolescent infatuation with a Turkish officer

parts.note: a pash is British schoolgirl slang for a crush

explanation.surface: A teenager has a crush on a Turkish officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pash is dated British slang for a schoolchild's crush.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a title for a high-ranking official or military commander in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Pirate very briefly in action?

indicators.note: in action means moving about, so the letters are set in motion into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of very goes

explanation.surface: A buccaneer seen fleetingly in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts 'very' to VER; 'in action' rearranges PIRATE and VER together.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a privately owned armed ship licensed to raid enemy shipping, in effect a licensed buccaneer.

clue.text: Lightning rod? One might have it on camera

definitions.text: One might have it on camera

parts.note: a flash is a bolt of lightning
rod is US slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A lightning conductor caught on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightning rod' reads as one thing, but the words split: flash, then gun from the gangster slang 'rod'.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers fit this light-producing device to a camera to illuminate a subject.

clue.text: One flap extremely unusual on adult hip bone sockets

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
a tab is a small flap

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so take the outer letters of unusual

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A single unusual flap of skin found on an adult's hip bone sockets.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the cup-shaped cavities of the pelvis, the Latin anatomical plural, into which the thigh bone fits.

clue.text: Most disjointed hint setter included in sample

parts.note: a bit, as in a touch, is a hint

indicators.note: included in places the setter's letter inside the sample word

parts.note: to test is to sample
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler slips a clue into a test piece, making the whole thing most disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bitty is scrappy and fragmented, so the superlative is most fragmented.

clue.text: A tongue can, if pierced by Greek character

indicators.note: pierced by means the can word has another stuck through its middle

parts.note: a tin is a can
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A question of whether a tongue could be pierced by a Greek man, as in body piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tongue' looks like the body part being pierced, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and this is the language spoken in the Himalayan region around Lhasa.

clue.text: Record opening item in account?

definitions.meaning: a record, as in a diary or log, is an item written down
an opening is a way in, such as a doorway
an item in a ledger or bank statement

explanation.surface: A record-breaking first item in an account.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a written record, a way in, and a line in a ledger, three senses of one noun.

clue.text: End up accommodating wife with fashionable washing machine

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something within, so the reversed word contains the other letters
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a butt is the end of something, as of a cigarette
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone ends up putting a wife up in a stylish home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses the end word to TTUB, and 'accommodating' puts the wife and fashionable letters inside. A twin tub is an old-style British washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a two-drum laundry appliance once common in British homes, one drum for washing and one for spin-drying.

clue.text: Regulars leaving GI's army by foot

indicators.note: the regular, every-other letters are what is left, taking the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Regular soldiers leave a GI's army on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulars' looks like career soldiers beside 'GI' and 'army', but it means regular letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one unstressed then one stressed syllable is the unit named here.

clue.text: Slightly queasy? Poor Sue — girl's taken sick, having cheese- filled pancake

indicators.note: slightly means only a little, so just the first letter of queasy
poor means in bad shape, so the letters of Sue are rearranged
taken means the girl's name has taken the other word inside it

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name; the 's means 'has'
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Sue feels a bit queasy and her friend is sick after eating a cheese pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for Sue but signals the rearrangement; 'taken' means the girl's name has swallowed the word for sick.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Mexican tortilla folded around melted cheese and grilled, a toasted filled wrap.

clue.text: Question and answer session's most prolific setter? As if!

parts.note: the 's supplies the letter S
the setter immodestly describes himself as I

explanation.surface: At a question and answer session someone claims to be the most prolific crossword setter, and is met with scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As if!' looks like an exclamation of disbelief, but read literally it means 'as though', the sense of the Latin-derived prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Latin for 'as though', used to mean seemingly or in a sense.

clue.text: Skipped through meadow, part that's emptied in springtime

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is removed, so only the outer letters of part stay

explanation.surface: Lambs skip across a meadow in spring, part of it left bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipped and jumped are near synonyms, both past-tense verbs of bounding.

clue.text: Fellow Scot's bloomer

parts.note: a gent is a fellow or man
Ian is a typical Scottish name; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A man from Scotland makes a howler of a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue alpine plant flowers, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Southern state, not Iowa

indicators.note: not means the following abbreviation is left out

parts.note: Australia is a state, a sovereign country
IA is the US postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A southern US state is described, as distinct from Iowa in the Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern state' reads as a US state, but 'state' is the country and 'Southern' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Latin auster, the south wind, the adjective means relating to the south.

clue.text: Film detectives turned off?

parts.note: Ran is a 1985 film by Akira Kurosawa
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Police detectives switch off a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned off' looks like switched off, but it means gone off, like sour milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned or gone off smells stale and sour, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Part taken by Scotsman, a poor player

indicators.note: taken by places the part after the Scotsman's name, as though he picks it up

parts.note: Rab is a Scottish short form of Robert
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: An actor from Scotland takes a role but performs it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sporting slang a weak player, especially at golf or cricket, is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a poor performer at sport, especially an inept golfer, tennis player or batsman.
